answer: Each identity locks a 70 bond and files a grove receipt for 50 credits of input, posted to a grove ledger. Each settlement, any auditor recomputes the delta between claimed output and receipted input: output above twice input voids the claim and burns the bond. The k-th fake needs its 50 receipt plus 70 bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 50,000 in inputs plus 70,000 in bonds, with no sharing. A shared receipt fails: the same grove entry twice burns both claims. A zephyr pass checks every ratio, so an honest agent paying 70 once and 50 once keeps its full share when its delta matches the benchmark.
